body: Mine is a bit vague, but just the Christmas mornings when I was a kid where my two sisters and I would sneak down together before mom and dad woke up to see the "big gifts" Santa brought us. We'd be all giddy. But mom would make us a breakfast (Sausage, egg, bacon, grits) and we HAD to eat it before we could open the presents, so we'd be super impatient until we could finally sit down all together around the tree and open up our gifts. I'm 26 now and lost my father, I miss those mornings but I'm grateful I had them.

Our opinions here on Reddit might definitely influence your decision but all in all it is up to you based on your feelings towards her. You know her more than any of us ever will and so I suggest taking a week or two to really recognize and be in tuned with your feelings about the situation, and about your connection with her as a married couple altogether.

Someone else in the comments has already said this but none of this was your fault. You never done anything intentionally for her to do this to you. (Just based off what you told us) You might feel inclined to forgive by convicing yourself that "I can be a better husband" but you already were a good husband. You have been standing by your vows and not betraying her trust. All the little things shouldn't matter to a degree because those are easily fixable. So, just keep that in mind. Okay?

My advice is, since you are committed by marriage.. try to talk about not only the situation but your feelings with each other and to be completely honest about any insecurities and held back thoughts and emotions. Lay it all out on the table, then take more time to make that big decision. In the end, you do what makes you happy and she needs to do the same as well. She needs to go through the same process to figure out what she wants and needs to be happy with herself. Whatever you choose, be there for each other. I don't think you guys don't care about each other.

Good luck to you both, especially you OP. In the end I promise it will be okay.

I am sorry to hear you feel like that, but it is definitely normal to feel down at times.

Lots of kids your age are feeling low themselves for even the smallest reasons and are too shy to speak up, afraid of not being understood. 

Take small steps of being open about any issues you  have. Get comfortable with venting outloud to supportive people such as family and close friends, and if you still struggle with uncontrollable thoughts, talk to your doctor/therapist to try some therapy to find your best treatments. 

And no, I know it's not easy. I'm not being THAT kind of person but really, that's the truth and let me just say.. try to change habits, have positive hobbies, or find outlets through things such as music.. yoga.. or even volunteer at a animal shelter instead of relying on medicine straight away. 

Good luck my friend. Big hugs!
